products.year: Unknown (Classic line ongoing since 1930s; current PEtec spec since ~2010s)

materials.spec: ~0.5% C, ~15% Cr, plus Mo and V; hardened to 58 HRC
Injection-molded black synthetic scales, tight molecular structure

materials.n: Stainless steel rivets (some SKUs listed as brass)
materials.spec: Three exposed rivets fixing scales to tang
materials.why: Official Wüsthof page states rivets are stainless steel; one third-party spec sheet for a different SKU lists brass, so material may vary by batch/model

materials.spec: Small aluminum ring fixed to tang under handle, corrodes preferentially to protect tang from moisture ingress

sourcing.why: Wüsthof states steel is 'specially formulated German steel' worked entirely at its Solingen plant, implying domestic melt/supply
sourcing.note: Exact steel mill/supplier name not publicly disclosed
Manufacturer does not disclose POM resin supplier or country of polymer manufacture

sourcing.why: Official page describes rivet fixing as part of the same Solingen manufacturing process described for the whole knife
sourcing.note: No named rivet supplier; brass listed on one competing spec sheet suggests possible variant

sourcing.why: Wüsthof describes the anode as its own patented invention, implying in-house production at its Solingen facility

construction.auto: Both: robotic/laser precision steps for forging, grinding, and edge-sharpening combined with manual hand-buffing/polishing and assembly
construction.tol: Laser-guided edge sharpened to ~14 degrees per side (28 degrees inclusive); tang/bolster ground to precision profile

steps.p: Upset forging of a single steel billet into blade, integral bolster, and full tang
Heat treatment/hardening of forged blank to 58 HRC
Grinding/profiling of blade geometry, then hand buffing and polishing of surface
Laser-guided PEtec computer-controlled edge sharpening to ~14 degrees per side
Injection-molding of POM scales; assembly onto tang with sacrificial anode and three rivets

skill.basis: Combination of laser/robotic precision steps and manual hand-finishing (buffing, polishing, assembly) documented by manufacturer and retailer spec sheets
skill.why: Manufacturer and retailer pages describe manual hand-buffing, polishing and assembly stages, but neither states a skill tier or training requirement — the tier is inferred from the operations they describe.
ops: Skilled forge operator judgment during upset forging of blade/tang/bolster
Manual craftsman finishing of forged blade surface for uniform shine
Technician sets up/monitors laser-guided PEtec sharpening system
Trained assembler aligns POM scales, anode, and rivets for seamless tang fit

parts.fail: Edge chipping on bone/frozen food; rust if chronically neglected despite stainless formulation
Surface wear/scratching over decades; not typically prone to cracking

parts.m: Stainless steel (or brass on some SKUs)
parts.fail: Loosening or scale separation from tang over very long-term heavy use
parts.why: Rivets are the sole mechanical fastener between tang and scales per official description

parts.fail: Anode designed to slowly dissolve over decades by design, protecting tang from corrosion

issues: Some retail units reportedly lacked 'Solingen Germany' country-of-origin marking on blade/box, per a user-reported bladeforums thread
Rivet material inconsistency across sources/SKUs: official brand page states stainless steel, one third-party spec sheet lists brass
Exact upstream suppliers for steel billet and POM resin are not publicly disclosed by the manufacturer
